Hi Sahil / Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a concrete proposal so we can kick off the customer-specific evals next week: 

1) Goal (what we agreed on): validate model fit for clinical triage summarization and structured extraction across your notes pipeline. We should measure: extraction accuracy (entity-level), end-to-end summarization usefulness (human-rated), and latency/throughput on your target p95 SLA.

2) Recommended model candidates (to run in parallel):
   - redwood-sdx-7b-q3 (fast, low-cost baseline)
   - redwood-sdx-13b-q4f16 (recommended balance of quality/latency)
   - redwood-sdx-70b-int8 (quality ceiling; expect higher cost)

3) Immediate deliverables from Redwood:
   - Eval runner config that consumes a JSONL test set (schema below) from S3 and spits out per-example predictions + automatic metrics.
   - Prompt set and template (attached: nyhealth_prompts.jsonl).
   - Shared scoring sheet with automatic dashboards (link above).

4) What we need from NyHealth by Wed 02/25 EOD:
   - A de-identified JSONL test set (<=5k examples for first pass) or a 500-example stratified sample if full dataset redaction timing is longer. See sample format in this thread.
   - Pass/fail thresholds you care about (suggested: extraction F1 >= 0.88 on critical entities; human summary preference >= 60% over baseline).
   - Confirmation you can upload to s3://redwood-evals/nyhealth/inputs-v1/ or grant us temporary read access.

5) Timeline: kickoff eval run Thu 02/26, initial metrics by Fri 02/27, short sync Mon 03/01 to review results and next experiment plan.

Attachments: nyhealth_prompts.jsonl (prompt templates + expected output parsing rules), sample_dataset_schema.jsonl.txt (example record).

If this looks right, please reply with dataset timing and any adjustments to thresholds.

Thanks — great questions. Quick answers and more detail on the scoring/runbook: 

1) Human eval methodology: pairwise blind preference tests. We sample ~300 summaries (stratified by note length / triage severity) and show reviewers two anonymized outputs (model vs baseline) with the reference note and a 7-point usefulness scale. Recommended sample: 300 gives decent power to detect ~10-12% preference gaps. We can scale to 500 if you want tighter CI.

2) Automatic metrics: for extraction we run span-level F1 and exact-match on critical entities, plus micro/macro F1. For summarization we produce ROUGE-L and BERTScore and also log token-level hallucination heuristics (entity hallucination counts). We will publish per-example outputs in CSV and push summary dashboards to the Google Sheet (link in metadata).

3) Dataset format (required JSONL schema; see attached sample_dataset_schema.jsonl.txt):
   - id: string (unique)
   - source_text: string (raw note text, de-identified)
   - annotations: {"entities": [{"type": "string", "start": int, "end": int, "text": "string"}], "summary": "string"} (for gold refs)
   - split: string ("eval" / "train" / "holdout")

Example record (single-line JSONL):
{"id":"ex-0001","source_text":"Patient reports intermittent chest pain...","annotations":{"entities":[{"type":"symptom","start":15,"end":31,"text":"intermittent chest pain"}],"summary":"..."},"split":"eval"}

4) S3 path: we can point Redwood eval runner at your bucket if you grant the redwood-evals IAM role read access. Copying into our managed bucket is optional but speeds up runs when there are transfer restrictions — your S3 path is fine if access policy allows it.

5) Pass/fail mechanics: we recommend using soft gates for the first run (report-only) then a hard gate on the second run after tuning. We'll instrument regression alerts for any model variant that drops >3 pts extraction F1 vs the baseline.

6) Next steps: please share the sample JSONL to s3://nyhealth-sharing/nyh-evals/sample-1k.jsonl by Wed 02/25 EOD and confirm the IAM role (redwood-evals@redwood). Karthik will stand up the eval job and send a dry-run log before we run at scale.

Attachments included in this message: nyhealth_eval_spec.xlsx (detailed metric definitions + scoring rubrics).

Best,
Marcus

Quick technical note before we kick: 

- Model variants: if latency at p95 < 400ms is a hard SLA, start with redwood-sdx-7b-q3 and redwood-sdx-13b-q4f16 in the first run. The 70b gives best quality but expect 2x cost and higher p95.
- Quantization: our runner supports q4f16 and int8. For extraction tasks q4f16 tends to preserve entity fidelity with good cost. We'll log token-level confidence to help you tune thresholds.
- Eval config: I'll upload the eval job JSON (config) to the same S3 folder and kick a dry run today. Expect a short Slack update when the dry-run completes.
